explain.say: Shanghai, Mumbai and Lagos sit on soft ground near water, yet tall towers rise there. The trick is piles: long columns driven or bored deep into the earth. The Burj Khalifa stands on about one hundred and ninety piles, each one and a half metres across. On the board, a single concrete pile, half a metre wide and fifteen metres long, in soft clay.

explain.say: Look at the forces. The load pushes down from the cap. The soil fights back in two ways: friction all along the shaft, called skin friction, and a push on the bottom, called end bearing. In soft clay, most of the help comes from the sides. Which arrow do you expect to be bigger?

explain.say: Skin friction! For clay we use the alpha method: shaft friction equals an adhesion factor, alpha, times the clay's undrained strength, times the shaft's surface area. With alpha of zero point five, strength fifty kilopascals and a shaft area of pi times zero point five times fifteen, that is about five hundred and eighty nine kilonewtons.

explain.say: Now the toe. End bearing in clay is nine times the strength there, a hundred kilopascals, times the base area, zero point one nine six square metres: about a hundred and seventy seven kilonewtons. Together the ultimate capacity is about seven hundred and sixty six. With a safety factor of two point five, each pile can safely carry about three hundred and six.

explain.say: Engineers check these sums on site with a pile load test: load a real pile and measure how far it sinks. Piles usually work in groups joined by a cap, and in sand the end bearing often matters more. Excellent work! Challenge: if the pile were thirty metres long in the same clay, roughly how big would its skin friction be?

faq.a: A pile is a long slender column of concrete, steel or timber, driven or bored into the ground to carry loads down to deeper, stronger soil or rock. Piles are used where surface soils are too weak.

faq.q: What is skin friction on a pile?
faq.a: Skin friction, or shaft resistance, is the grip between the soil and the sides of the pile along its length. In soft clay it usually provides most of the capacity.
End bearing is the resistance at the pile tip as it presses on the soil or rock below. It matters most when the pile sits on a strong layer like dense sand or rock.
asks: What is base resistance of a pile?

faq.q: How do you calculate pile capacity in clay?
faq.a: Add shaft and base resistance. Shaft: alpha times c u times the shaft area; base: 9 times c u at the tip times the base area. For our pile, 589 plus 177 is about 766 kilonewtons ultimate.

faq.q: What is a pile load test?
faq.a: A pile load test applies increasing load to a real pile, often against kentledge or reaction piles, and measures settlement. It confirms the design capacity on site.

facts: The Burj Khalifa's foundation uses 192 bored piles, each 1.5 metres in diameter.
In the alpha method, pile shaft resistance in clay is α × c_u × shaft area, with α typically between about 0.3 and 1.
